starting_points.name: Android Studio Empty Activity template
starting_points.when: Creating a new Kotlin/Jetpack Compose Android app with Android Studio, an installed compatible SDK/JDK and a new destination.
steps: Record application ID/namespace, minimum SDK, target devices and release ownership. Choose a source workspace outside synchronized storage.
In Android Studio use New Project from the welcome screen or File > New > New Project. Select the phone/tablet Empty Activity template for Compose.
Set the app name, package, save location and required minimum SDK; use Kotlin. Finish the wizard and allow dependency resolution/Gradle sync to complete.

Record Android Studio/template version and generated options. Inspect the generated wrapper, Gradle scripts, version catalog if supplied, manifest, activity, resources and test source sets before adding app behavior.
notes: Preserve the generated compatible toolchain/dependency combination initially; verify the selected SDK and JDK. A fixed minimum SDK copied from a tutorial does not replace the product's support requirements.

For existing projects, open/import the current project and inspect its modules and variants; do not run a new-project generator over it. gradle init --type kotlin-application creates a Kotlin/JVM command-line app, not an Android/Compose application.

starting_points.name: Official Android CLI project templates
starting_points.when: Creating a new Compose app without IDE interaction, when the current official Android CLI is installed and its create help/template listing confirms support.
steps: Obtain the Android CLI from the official Android developer tools page, complete its documented SDK/JDK prerequisites and record its installed version.
Inspect create help and available templates. The reviewed reference documents an empty Compose activity default when no template is supplied; verify this in the installed release before creation.
Run creation into a new or empty destination using the agreed identity and minimum SDK. Inspect generated files and run the baseline checks before customizing.

commands.purpose: Record the installed official Android CLI version after installation.
Verify current creation flags and default template behavior.
List the installed official templates without creating a project.
Create the documented default Compose template after confirming the installed CLI's default and replacing all placeholders.

notes: The current official documentation offers this CLI route; it is distinct from obsolete Android SDK android commands. Never use --force to scaffold into an existing app.
Reviewed pages differ in example template spelling, so this recipe uses the documented default and requires installed help/list verification instead of guessing a template identifier.

If neither the official CLI nor Android Studio project wizard is accessible, report the missing prerequisite and request a generated baseline/operator handoff. Do not silently hand-scaffold Gradle and Android configuration.

follow_up_generators.name: Android Studio component and module templates
follow_up_generators.when: An existing project needs another compatible activity, Compose component, resource or module.
notes: Right-click the intended package/folder in the Project window and select New, or use File > New. Select an applicable template, configure it and inspect all generated changes after Gradle sync.

Use New Module for a new app/library module only when the architecture requires it; do not create another activity for every Compose screen. Review manifest registrations, resource names and target module dependencies.

follow_up_generators.name: Generated wrapper verification
follow_up_generators.when: After project generation/sync, with a compatible JDK/SDK; discover the actual module and variant before substituting placeholders.

commands.purpose: Verify the generated Gradle wrapper and active JVM; use gradlew.bat on Windows.
Discover actual modules before choosing the application module.
Discover tasks and variants before selecting build/test commands.
Lint, unit-test and build the discovered debug application variant; adapt task suffixes for actual variants.
Run instrumentation/Compose tests after starting a compatible emulator or connecting an authorized device; adapt the variant.

notes: These commands consume the generated project; they are not app generators. Review task availability before running, especially with product flavors or nonstandard module names.

Use the generated version catalog when present; when adding dependencies, centralize compatible versions and sync/build. A wrapper or catalog alone does not prove AGP/JDK/Kotlin/Compose compatibility.

preserve: Keep generated gradlew/gradlew.bat and gradle/wrapper files, settings and module build scripts, gradle.properties, version catalog when present, and repository configuration; record intentional deviations.
Keep the app manifest, Kotlin activity/Compose theme, resources and generated unit/instrumentation test setup until deliberate product changes replace them.

Retain generated ignore rules and extend them for workspace needs; exclude local.properties, SDK paths, caches/build outputs, private signing keys and .DS_Store without ignoring the wrapper JAR or source/resources.
verification: Record which official template and tool version created the project, its identity/minimum SDK choices, and the generated dependency/toolchain baseline.
Confirm wrapper files and application source sets are included in version control; review Git's candidate file set and ignore behavior without changing an existing user's index.
Run the discovered lint/unit/build tasks, then instrumentation tests with an emulator/device; inspect reports and distinguish missing environment prerequisites from failing app checks.
Template generation and a debug build do not establish signed release readiness, production architecture or complete accessibility; complete the profile's product/device/release checks.

integration_steps: Record package/application identity, minimum and target SDKs, supported form factors, API contract, permissions and release owner; verify the generated toolchain matches these requirements.

Use the generated Gradle wrapper and record compatible JDK, SDK, Gradle, AGP, Kotlin and Compose versions. Maintain dependency/plugin versions in the project version catalog when present; introduce catalog changes deliberately in existing builds.
Implement screen state and ViewModels behind repositories. Add Room migrations, a typed HTTP client and deterministic fake data. Keep secrets out of version control and app resources.
Run discovered JVM test, lint and debug build tasks. Start a documented emulator or connect an authorized device, then run instrumentation and Compose checks.
Exercise process death, offline/reconnect, rotation, permission denial, TalkBack, large fonts and every supported form factor on appropriate devices.

Have the account owner establish package ownership, upload-key custody and Play App Signing. Follow the authorized release workflow to build a signed bundle and verify internal-track install/update; retain reports and distribution receipts. Build success is not store publication.
